title: HCP — Request Grant — payload
description: A Context Client asks an HCP Provider for a grant over a person's context, naming what it needs as HCP authorization details (HCP 6.1.5; RFC 9396 `authorization_details` of the HCP type, as HCP 13.3 names them). HCP Core defines no grant-request operation (HCP 6.1.7 leaves it to the profiles), so this task carries no HCP operation: it is a Trust-Task-native authenticated channel in the sense of HCP 6.1.6 and 12.2. The person decides out of band; while they do, the provider answers with trust-task-next-step. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

access.description: What the client asks to be granted: one or more HCP authorization details (HCP 6.1.5 `access`, HCP 13.3). The provider shows each to the person before they act (HCP 6.1.6). The maxItems of 16 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

grantType.description: The kind of grant the client asks for (HCP 6.1.4). Absent means `temporary`, HCP's default. `persistent` only lets the person be offered persistence as a separate affirmative act; it never pre-selects it (HCP 6.1.4), and the grant is temporary unless the person elects otherwise. Pending HCP confirmation.

expiresIn.description: For a temporary grant, the lifetime the client asks for, in seconds. Absent means HCP's default of 4 hours; HCP's maximum is 24 hours (HCP 6.1.3). The provider MAY grant less and never more. Ignored for a persistent grant.

subjectHint.description: An identifier by which the provider can find the person whose context is asked for, and reach them to decide — the counterpart of OpenID Connect `login_hint`. Absent where the provider serves one person only. The provider never says whether it knows the hint (see the specification's Errors). Pending HCP confirmation.

requestingParty.description: HCP `requestingParty` (HCP 3.4, 6.1.5): the person or organization on whose behalf the client asks, where it differs from the Context Subject. Shown to the person before they act (HCP 6.1.6).

AccessRequest.description: One HCP authorization detail as requested (HCP 6.1.5, 13.3).

actions.description: HCP `actions`: what the client may do with the categories. `provenance` only alongside `read` (HCP 6.1.5, 7.4.1).

categories.description: HCP `categories` the detail covers (HCP 4.5, 6.1.5). The maxItems of 256 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

purposes.description: HCP `purposes` the client asks to use the categories for (HCP 6.1.5.2). Absent means the person chooses them before approving (HCP 6.1.5.2, 13.3). The maxItems of 32 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

narrowedTo.description: HCP `narrowedTo` (HCP 6.1.5.1): implementation-defined keys that only narrow. A key the provider does not support is refused with malformedRequest (HCP 6.1.5.1 rule 2).

onwardSharing.description: HCP `onwardSharing` (HCP 3.12, 6.1.4, 6.1.5): asks that the person be offered onward sharing for this detail, as a separate act after they confirm the grant. Only in a detail that includes `read` and whose categories are all of Low default sensitivity; otherwise malformedRequest (HCP 6.1.5).

GrantAction.description: An HCP grant action (HCP 6.1.5). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

RequestedPurpose.description: An HCP purpose (HCP 6.1.5.2): a code and a description the person can read.

description.description: What the purpose means, in words the person can read. The provider shows its own description where it has one. The maxLength, the same as the shared grant's purpose description, is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

OnwardSharingRequest.description: A request for onward sharing (HCP 6.1.5). `notTo` is set by the provider, never asked for.

domains.description: DNS domains the client proposes to limit onward sharing to. The person may narrow them further (HCP 6.1.4).

id.description: HCP `requestingParty.id`: an identifier for the party.

name.description: HCP `requestingParty.name`: a name the person can recognize, shown before they act (HCP 6.1.6).

Response.title: HCP — Request Grant — response payload
Response.description: The person approved: the grant evidence, as HCP's OAuth token response carries it (HCP 13.3, 13.4), and the grant as approved, as HCP's grant object (HCP 6.1.5). Sent only after the person's affirmative act (HCP 6.1.6); while they decide the provider answers trust-task-next-step, and a decline is trust-task-error permissionDenied — never this shape.

accessToken.description: The HCP access token for the new grant (the token response's `access_token`, HCP 13.3), opaque to the client. The client presents it unchanged as `accessToken` in hcp/entries/query and every other hcp/* task it sends under the grant. Its lifetime follows HCP 13.4 (default 1 hour, at most 24 hours). The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

tokenExpiresAt.description: When `accessToken` stops being accepted (the token response's `expires_in`, HCP 13.4, as an instant), in whole seconds. Never after the grant's `expiresAt`.

grant.description: The grant as the person approved it, as HCP's grant object (HCP 6.1.5) and as hcp/grants/read-own returns it: `access` may be narrower than asked (HCP 13.3: the token response carries the authorization details granted), `status` is `active`, and `expiresAt` is null for a persistent grant. `authorizingPrincipal.delegation` is withheld, as from any Context Client reading its own grant (HCP 17.4).
